newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firmer as refiners come out in the cold.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firmer as refiners come out in the cold.

text.p: Brent crude oil outright values soared with futures on forecasts of colder weather, easing some pressure off physical barrels which started to move as refiners began to dip into the market after a hiatus, dealers said.
December Brent was talked around $22.60 a barrel in the late afternoon after trading earlier at $22.37 a barrel. Intermonth spreads were slighly firmer with a Dec/Jan trade at +33 cents.

Dated Brent remained at a sharp discount to December paper as an overhang of physical North Sea barrels and a closed U.S. arb depressed the wet market although some grades recovered as the Brent contango shrank.
A major sold a Brent cargo due to load Nov 22-24 to a French oil company for Dec Brent -35 cents after selling a Nov 15-17 cargo at Dec Brent -54 cents on Thursday.
Improved refinery margins on continued products strength and interest from the Far East for both crude and products was also supportive, traders said.
One million barrels of Ekofisk loading Nov 20 traded at Dated Brent +5 cents to a French oil company. The gasoline-rich grade traded on Wednesday at Dated +10 cents for an end-November loader.

"The arb is not open, there is a wet overhang but refineries are coming in to buy. There is a bit of panic going on and some of them waited so long that they now fear they may have missed the boat," a wet trader said.
"I still believe the market has to consume the overhang before going higher," he added.

The CFD market showed Dated Brent was valued at -33 cents for next week. The four Brent dates which turned wet on Friday were all kept by oil companies amid some unconfirmed talk that one of them was planning to ship cargoes transatlantic.
